messages:
morgan: Quick q — I ran a perfetto/nsys sweep on the QPS regression and I think we need a simple range taxonomy for runtime traces. The current NVTX ranges are too coarse to attribute stalls across kernel-selection + KV cache misses.
liam: +1, can you paste the trace snippet?
priya: Agree. We've been blind when kernel fallback happens due to quantization path selection.
morgan: Here's a short excerpt from the nsys capture (trimmed):
```
nsys profile --sample=none --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --output=run1
# kernel timeline: matmul_q8 (36ms) -> kv_prefetch (4ms) -> matmul_q8_fallback (48ms)
# noticed repeated pattern when kv cache miss ratio > 0.2
```
dan: Oof, that fallback spike looks like kernel-selector decided against the fused kv-prefetch matmul. Maybe our heuristic threshold is wrong.
kyra: We should add per-request NVTX spans with metadata like kernel_hint and kv_hit_ratio so perf scripts can group by those attrs.
eva: For naming, can we standardize: `req/<req_id>/phase/<phase_name>[:attr=value...]` ? Example: `req/abc123/phase/kv_prefetch:hit=true`
liam: I like a compact scheme. Suggestion: `r:<req_id>|s:<span>|k:<kernel>` — shorter for perfetto flame viewers.
priya: Important: don't leak PII in req_id. Use hashed ids in traces.
perf-bot: perf-regression-detected: p99 latency +12% vs baseline (2026-03-01). Affected route: /generate (small-batch).
morgan: Proposal: new NVTX ranges we add in runtime: 1) `r:<id>|s:request` (top-level), 2) `r:<id>|s:kv_prefetch|k:<kernel_hint>|hit:<0|1>`, 3) `r:<id>|s:compute|k:<selected_kernel>|q:<quant>` 4) `r:<id>|s:post_process`
dan: Can we also push attributes separately so tools that parse events can index them? e.g. NVTXPayload with keys kv_hit_ratio, seq_len, batch_size.
kyra: Yes. Example instrumentation snippet for C++ runtime: 
```cpp
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH_EX("r:" + hid(req.id) + "|s:kv_prefetch|k:" + kernel_hint);
nvtxEventAttributes_t attr = {0};
attr.version = NVTX_VERSION; attr.size = NVTX_EVENT_ATTRIB_STRUCT_SIZE;
attr.payload.type = NVTX_PAYLOAD_TYPE_UNSIGNED_INT;
attr.payload.value.u = (uint32_t)(kv_hit ? 1 : 0);
nvtxEventRegister(&attr);
// ... prefetch logic ...
NVTX_RANGE_POP();
```
eva: Small nit: nvtxEventRegister creates global events; prefer nvtxRangeStartEx + metadata as name string to avoid registry explosion.
liam: Good catch. Name-encoding may get long though; perf tools truncate. We should include a short encoded suffix and then emit a JSON blob to a sidecar log for full details.
priya: For batching heuristics: add `s:batch_coalesce` span showing original batch size vs sent batch size. That will help quantify how often continuous batching collapses requests.
morgan: Also add a KV cache diagnostic span when we fall back to disk/host memory: `s:kv_slowpath` and include io_latency_ms attribute.
dan: For kernel selection traceability, we need to record both the requested kernel_hint and the actual kernel entry. e.g. two ranges: `s:kernel_hint` then `s:kernel_exec`. That will make the difference explicit in timelines.
kyra: Any objections to the naming alphabet? want to avoid too many colons `:` because some tools parse them. Maybe use pipe `|` as separator and `=` for pairs. Example: `r=abc|s=kv_prefetch|k=matmul_q8|hit=0`
morgan: I prefer the pipe+equals form. Let's standardize to `r=<hash>|s=<span>|k=<kernel>|hit=<0|1>|b=<batch>`
liam: OK. Action items: 
- morgan: add instrumentation PR with helper macros and an example mapping for performance tests (ETA 2d)
- priya: extend perf analysis script to group traces by `k` and `hit` attributes (ETA 3d)
- dan: run a dedicated nsys sweep with kv-miss injection once the spans are in (ETA after PR)
perf-bot: created perf-issue #1429 and tagged eng-runtime :rotating_light:
priya: One more thought — add a sampling knob to avoid tracing every request in high QPS env. e.g. trace 0.1% by default and 100% on canary.
eva: sounds good. Also add a lint check for span name length in CI to avoid accidental OOM in perf viewers.
morgan: I'll open the PR with the proposed naming, snippets and a sample perfetto profile. Thanks all! :thumbsup:
